title: Re:Monster
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Tomokui Kanata is murdered and reborn as a goblin with his memories and the power to gain abilities from whatever he eats. As Gobrou he devours monsters and enemies, rises to lead his tribe, takes several wives including human women the tribe abducted, and later founds a mixed-race mercenary company. The story follows his evolution through stronger monster forms and growing power.
life_message: It holds up strength, appetite and building your own tribe as the way to thrive in a brutal world.

content.note: Constant lethal fights; elders beaten to death as example; hero eats defeated foes (Wikipedia; Suitable for Treatment review).
Grim tone but an unbeatable hero (review).
Abducted women held for breeding, a harem, and goblins allowed to rape drugged elves, told matter-of-factly (review; Wikipedia; AniList Female Harem; MangaDex suggestive).
Kidnapping and coercion within the tribe go unpunished (Wikipedia; review).

dominant: Survival of the strongest; consuming to evolve; tribal expansion

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Status is won by defeating rivals personally; challenges are answered with force.

Order vs freedom.evidence: Tribal law is whatever the strongest decides; Gobrou acts as he pleases.

Civic vs kin.evidence: Brood brothers, wives and children are Gobrou's whole world.

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Rank in the tribe follows strength and evolution tier.

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Pragmatic, game-like logic of leveling up; gods exist but guide little.

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Eat or be eaten survival drives everything.

folkways.japan: Game-like leveling, reincarnation into a monster and a household-building harem reflect Japanese web-novel isekai conventions.

delivery.evidence: Sean Gaffney (Suitable for Treatment) calls it a power fantasy with matter-of-fact narration that does not reflect on captives' treatment.
delivery.note: The narration presents the strong winning as normal and gives no space to the views of prey or captives.

winners_losers: Gobrou and his tribe win by strength; prey, rivals and captive women lose. Sympathy goes to the strongest.
